title: Henri Coanda's 1936 saucer patent and Project Y consulting
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Henri Coanda's 1936 saucer patent and Project Y consulting, about 1936; 1950s at Vichy France; Wright-Patterson AFB, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: >> He had basically the first patent on a flying saucer in 1936.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, speaking with a writer named Peter Levenda, says that an inventor named Henri Coanda had basically the first patent on a flying saucer, in 1936. The story links Coanda to Vichy France and later to consulting on a saucer-related effort called Project Y, tied to Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, a US Air Force site, which would suggest saucer-shaped craft had human roots in secret engineering work.
